seo_title: NCLT: EPFO Can't Recover Dues From Spent Guarantor Estate
title: NCLT Hyderabad: EPFO Cannot Recover PF Dues From a Personal Guarantor's Already-Distributed Bankruptcy Estate
case_name: Central Board of Trustees, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation v. Dommeti Surya Rama Krishna Sai Baba & Ors.
citation: I.A. No. 1288 of 2025 in C.P.(IB) No. 21/123/HDB/2023, order dated 06.11.2026
card_summary: EPFO sought about Rs 1.12 crore in provident fund dues from a personal guarantor's bankruptcy estate, citing statutory priority under the EPF Act and the IBC. NCLT Hyderabad dismissed the plea, holding the corporate debtor and its guarantor are separate legal persons, and that Part III IBC recovery is confined to the guarantor's own estate, already realised and distributed among creditors.
card_tip: A creditor with statutory priority against a corporate debtor cannot assume that priority carries over to a personal guarantor's separate bankruptcy estate once that estate is already exhausted and distributed.
verification_notes: The applicant (EPFO), the respondent's name, the case numbers (I.A. 1288 of 2025 in C.P.(IB) 21/123/HDB/2023), the order date of 6 November 2026, the GKC Projects resolution plan approval date of 30 March 2021, EPFO's reliance on Sections 8B-8G and 11 of the EPF Act and Sections 36(4)(a)(iii)/155(2) of the IBC, and the tribunal's holding that the corporate debtor and personal guarantor are distinct persons with the guarantor's estate already exhausted are all taken from LiveLaw Biz's report and from the first pages of the order PDF it hosts. This is the only outlet carrying the item that this run found; a second, independently-run outlet could not be located, so this draft rests on the LiveLaw Biz report read alongside the order text itself rather than two separate media reports. The approximate Rs 1.12 crore claim figure comes from the same report and was not cross-checked against a second source.
